app.name: Nostek Panel
login.title: Sign in
login.lead: Sign in to manage your server.
login2fa.title: Two-factor check
login2fa.lead: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app, or one recovery code.
setup.title: Create the first admin
setup.lead: This one-time link creates the administrator. Next you will set up two-factor sign-in.
enrol.title: Set up two-factor sign-in
enrol.step1: 1. Scan this QR code with an authenticator app.
enrol.manual: Or type this key by hand:
enrol.step2: 2. Enter the 6-digit code the app shows.
codes.title: Your recovery codes
codes.lead: Each code works once if you lose your phone. Store them in your password manager now; they are not shown again.
dash.codeslow: Fewer than 3 recovery codes left. Create new ones on your Profile page.
settings.tz.help: Every time in the panel is shown in this zone.
settings.codes.new: Create new codes (old ones stop working)
reveal.title: New admin password
reveal.lead: This link shows the new password once. Store it in your password manager before you leave this page.
linkgone.title: Link not valid
linkgone.lead: This link was already used or has expired. Ask for a new one on the server.
notfound.title: Not found
err.pwshort: The password must be at least 12 characters.
err.code: The code is not valid. Try the newest code.
err.toomany: Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again.
settings.theme.help: Light, dark, or follow your device. Saved on your account.
dash.sites.go: Add and manage websites: WordPress, Laravel, PHP and static sites.
sites.noagent: The site agent is not reachable, so websites cannot be shown or changed. Status is unknown, not OK. Install or start it with the SITE-01 package.
sites.trash.help: Deleted websites stay here with their files and database for 7 days, then they are removed for good.
sites.new.help: The domain may still point to another host. Then the website starts on its preview address, and the domain is connected after the move.
sites.php.eol: end of life, no security fixes
sites.aliases.help: Separate with spaces or commas. They redirect to the main address.
sites.title: Website title
sites.approve.lead: This creates the website %s. Nothing changes until you approve.
sites.creates.apache: Containers: Apache with PHP, MariaDB database. Own private network; only the web server is reachable through the edge.
sites.creates.nginx: Containers: Nginx, PHP-FPM, MariaDB database. Own private network; only Nginx is reachable through the edge.
sites.resources.apache: Up to 1 GB memory (512 MB web, 512 MB database); disk grows with the website.
sites.resources.nginx: Up to 1.1 GB memory (128 MB Nginx, 512 MB PHP, 512 MB database); disk grows with the website.
sites.undo.text: Delete moves the website to the trash for 7 days; it can be restored from there.
sites.job.wait: Usually 1 to 3 minutes. Progress updates by itself.
sites.job.failhelp: Nothing else was changed. You can delete the website from its page and try again.
sites.job.pwhelp: The password is shown one time only. Save it in your password manager right away.
sites.job.pwonce: Save this password now. It is not stored in the panel and cannot be shown again.
sites.job.pwgone: The admin password was already shown (or has expired). Use "Lost your password" in WordPress to set a new one.
sites.delete.help: Stops the website and moves it to the trash for 7 days. Type %s to confirm.
sites.delete.mismatch: The domain you typed does not match. Nothing was deleted.
sites.done.restore_failed: The website could not be restored. See the activity log.
profile.saved.pw: Password changed. Other devices are signed out.
profile.look.help: Theme and highlight colour. Saved on your account.
profile.pw.help: At least 12 characters. After the change, every other device is signed out.
err.pwsame: The new password must differ from the current one.
settings.moved.help: Theme, highlight colour, password and recovery codes are on your Profile page.
sites.step.now.pull images: Downloading images (the first site can take 1-2 minutes)…
stack.title: Stack
stack.help: The containers of this website. CPU and memory update by themselves every few seconds.
stack.err: The containers cannot be read right now:
files.title: File Manager
files.help: Files of this WordPress website (the folder served at its address). The database and the website's secrets are not in here and cannot be reached from here.
files.name: Name
files.delete.ask: Move %s to the trash? It can be restored for 7 days.
files.truncated: This folder has more than 5000 entries; only the first 5000 are shown.
files.upload.help: Up to %s per file. Uploading a .zip? Extract it here afterwards from its ⋯ menu.
files.upload.overwrite: Replace files with the same name
files.trash.help: Deleted files and folders stay here for 7 days, then they are removed for good.
files.trash.empty: Nothing deleted in the last 7 days.
files.save.help: Saving replaces the file at once; the old version is not kept.
files.edit.toobig: This file is larger than 2 MB, too large for the editor. Download it instead.
files.edit.binary: This is not a text file. Download it instead.
files.edit.wpconfig: wp-config.php holds the website's settings. A mistake here takes the website offline until it is fixed.
files.err.list: The folder could not be read:
files.err.name: Name is not valid (no / and not . or ..).
files.done.delete: Moved to the trash (restorable for 7 days).
db.title: Database
db.err: The database could not be read:
db.name: Database
db.user.help: (password stays in the website's secret file)
db.export.help: Downloads a fresh copy of the whole database as .sql.gz. The website keeps running.
db.import.help: Runs an .sql or .sql.gz file (up to 512 MB) against this database. A copy of the current database is taken first and kept, so the import can be undone.
db.import.confirm: I understand that tables in the file replace the ones in this database
db.import.type: Only .sql or .sql.gz files can be imported.
db.backups.help: The newest 3 are kept. Import one to undo an import.
db.sql.warn: Statements run at once on the live database and cannot be undone here. Download an export first if you are not sure.
db.sql.help: SELECT shows at most 1000 rows; long values are shortened.
db.sql.ok: Done. The statement returned no rows.
db.rows.help: Row counts of InnoDB tables are estimates.
db.done.import: Import finished. A copy from before the import is kept below.
wp.check.title: Integrity check result
wp.check.plugins.bad: Some plugins changed or could not be checked
wp.check.help: Compares files with the official checksums on wordpress.org. Premium or custom plugins have no checksums there and show as "could not be checked"; that is normal.
wp.cli.help: Runs one WP-CLI command in this site's own container (user www-data, no shell). Interactive commands (shell, db cli) and --ssh/--http/--path are not available. Time limit 3 minutes.
wp.err.name: Not a valid plugin or theme name.
wp.install.help: Enter the slug from the wordpress.org address, for example wordpress.org/plugins/wordfence → wordfence.
wp.item.name: Name
wp.login.title: Opening wp-admin
wp.login.help: This link works once and for 60 seconds. If it expired, press Log in to wp-admin again in the panel.
wp.sec.ssladmin: Login and wp-admin always over HTTPS
wp.sec.fileedit: File editor in wp-admin turned off
wp.sec.isolated: Site isolated in its own Docker stack (database not open to the internet)
wp.tls.until: valid until %s (%d days left), renewed automatically
wp.update.everything.ask: Update WordPress, every plugin and every theme now? Tip: export the database first in the Database tab.
wp.delete.plugin.ask: Delete plugin %s? It is deactivated, its data cleaned up and its files removed. This cannot be undone.
wp.delete.theme.ask: Delete theme %s? Its files are removed. This cannot be undone.
wp.set.debug.help: PHP errors go to the site Logs (never shown to visitors).
wp.set.indexing.help: Turn off while the site is still a draft so it stays out of Google.
wp.set.system_cron.help: Scheduled tasks run from the server every 5 minutes instead of on visits. Faster pages, tasks still on time.
wp.set.maintenance.help: Visitors see a "under maintenance" page (503); logged-in admins still see the site.
wp.err.read.plain: Usually the website is stopped or just starting. Start it from the Overview tab, wait a moment, then reload this page.
wp.warn.title: Some details could not be shown
wp.warn.part.plugins: The plugin list could not be read, so plugin updates may be missing.
wp.warn.part.themes: The theme list could not be read, so theme updates may be missing.
wp.warn.part.core: Checking for a newer WordPress failed (usually wordpress.org could not be reached).
wp.warn.part.other: Some other detail could not be read.
wp.warn.plain: The website keeps running and everything else still works. Reload this page later. If this keeps showing, send the technical details to your admin.
bak.title: Backup
bak.help: A backup is a complete copy of this website: every file and the whole database, in one archive. You can put the website back to any backup in this list.
bak.offsite: Backups are kept on this server, and every night at 03:30 WIB the server's off-site backup carries them to outside storage too.
bak.daily: Make a backup every day (after 02:00 WIB)
bak.schedule.help: Older daily backups are removed by themselves. Backups you make by hand are never removed automatically.
bak.none: No backup yet. Make the first one with the button above.
bak.err: The backup list could not be read right now. The website itself is not affected; try again in a minute.
bak.restore.warn: This puts the website back to how it was on %s. Changes made after that are replaced. A safety copy of the website as it is now is made first, so this can be undone.
bak.restore.mismatch: The typed domain does not match. Nothing was restored.
bak.delete.ask: Delete the backup of %s? This cannot be undone.
bak.job.wait: You can leave this page; the work goes on in the background.
bak.job.restored: The website is back. The state before the restore is kept as the safety copy %s.
bak.job.fail.backup: The backup could not be made. The website itself was not changed.
bak.job.fail.restore: The restore did not finish. If the website looks wrong, restore the newest safety copy in the list below.
bak.step.switch files: Website switched to the restored files
bak.step.now.safety database: Making a safety copy of the database…
bak.step.now.safety files: Making a safety copy of the files…
bak.step.now.switch files: Switching the website to the restored files…
bak.restore.title: Restore the backup of %s
sites.app.wordpress.help: Blog, company profile or shop, installed and ready to log in.
sites.app.php.help: Your own PHP code (plain PHP, CodeIgniter, Slim…), with a MariaDB database if you want one.
sites.app.static.help: HTML, or the built output of React, Vue, Svelte or Astro. No PHP, no database.
sites.title.optional: Optional: shown on the starter page.
sites.creates.php-apache: Containers: Apache with PHP. Own private network; only the web server is reachable through the edge.
sites.creates.php-nginx: Containers: Nginx and PHP-FPM. Own private network; only Nginx is reachable through the edge.
sites.creates.static: Container: Nginx serving your files read-only. Unknown paths fall back to index.html (for React/Vue routes).
sites.creates.db: Plus a MariaDB database on the private network.
sites.resources.php-apache: Up to 512 MB memory; disk grows with the website.
sites.resources.php-nginx: Up to 640 MB memory (128 MB Nginx, 512 MB PHP); disk grows with the website.
sites.resources.static: Up to 128 MB memory; disk grows with the website.
sites.resources.db: The database adds up to 512 MB.
sites.job.appnext: Your website is live with a starter page. Upload your site with the File Manager (a .zip can be extracted there), replacing the starter page.
sites.app.laravel.help: A fresh Laravel project with a MariaDB database, queue worker and scheduler, ready to use.
sites.creates.laravel: Containers: Nginx, PHP-FPM (Laravel image built from official images), queue worker, scheduler, MariaDB database. The latest Laravel is installed with Composer; the panel fills .env.
sites.resources.laravel: Memory up to 1.6 GB (Nginx 128 MB, PHP 512 MB, queue 256 MB, scheduler 256 MB, database 512 MB); disk grows with the website.
sites.step.now.build PHP image: Building the PHP image (1–3 minutes the first time)…
sites.job.laravelnext: Laravel is running. Change the code with the File Manager; after adding migrations, press Run migrate on the Overview.
lar.title: Laravel
lar.help: Artisan commands that are safe to run from the panel. Other commands cannot be run from here.
lar.env: App settings are in the .env file (File Manager). The database password is not in it: the panel hands it over from a secret file.
sites.app.node.help: Express, NestJS, Nuxt, SvelteKit or Next.js from your Git repository, built and started by the panel.
sites.creates.node: One container: your app on the official Node.js image, built from the branch you choose. Each deploy builds a new release; the live one keeps running until the new one answers.
sites.resources.node: Up to 768 MB memory while running (the build may use up to 1.5 GB and 2 CPUs for at most 15 minutes); disk grows with the website and the 3 kept releases.
node.repo.help: A public https address, for example https://github.com/user/app.git, or for a private repository an SSH address such as git@github.com:user/app.git (the panel then makes a deploy key for it).
node.help: The panel runs npm ci (or npm install without a lock file), then the build command, then the start command. Your app must listen on the port in the PORT environment value (3000). Empty fields use the defaults shown.
deploy.title: Deploy
deploy.help: Deploy fetches the newest commit of the branch and builds it next to the live release. The website switches only when the new release answers; if it does not, the previous release stays live. The last 3 good releases are kept for a rollback.
deploy.log.title: Build log of release #%d
deploy.log.help: Output of git, npm and your build command. Values from your environment file are not printed by the panel; your own scripts may print them.
deploy.failhelp: The website keeps running on its previous release. Open Deploy to read the build log of this release.
sites.job.nodenext: Your app is live. Push to the branch and press Deploy to publish a new version.
sites.done.rollback: The chosen release is live again.
sites.step.now.fetch and build: Fetching the source and building (npm install and build, a few minutes)…
sites.step.now.start new release: Starting the new release and waiting for it to answer…
node.source.files.help: The panel puts a small starter app in the source folder. Upload your app there with the File Manager (a .zip can be extracted), then press Deploy.
node.dir.help: Only when the app is in a subfolder, for example apps/web in a monorepo.
env.title: Environment values
env.help: Settings and secrets of your app (database address, API keys). The app gets them when it starts and the build gets them too. Values are never shown again after saving; saving restarts the app. Values the build uses (for example NEXT_PUBLIC_…) apply at the next deploy.
env.name: Name
sites.done.env-set: Value saved, the app restarted with it.
sites.done.env-delete: Value deleted, the app restarted without it.
sites.app.go.help: A Go web app (net/http, Gin, Echo, Fiber …) from your Git repository or your own files, built and started by the panel.
sites.app.python.help: Django, FastAPI or Flask from your Git repository or your own files, in its own virtual environment.
sites.creates.go: One container: your app on the official Go image, built with go build. Each deploy builds a new release; the live one keeps running until the new one answers.
sites.creates.python: One container: your app on the official Python image with its packages from requirements.txt in a virtual environment. Each deploy builds a new release; the live one keeps running until the new one answers.
sites.resources.go: Up to 768 MB memory while running (the build may use up to 1.5 GB and 2 CPUs for at most 15 minutes); disk grows with the website and the 3 kept releases.
sites.resources.python: Up to 768 MB memory while running (the build may use up to 1.5 GB and 2 CPUs for at most 15 minutes); disk grows with the website and the 3 kept releases.
go.help: The panel runs go mod download, then the build command (default: go build to ./server), then the start command (default ./server). Your app must listen on the port in PORT (3000).
python.help: The panel makes a virtual environment .venv and installs requirements.txt, then runs the build command (optional, for example collectstatic) and the start command, for example .venv/bin/gunicorn -b 0.0.0.0:$PORT app:app or .venv/bin/uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT. Your app must listen on PORT (3000).
sites.trash.remove.help: Delete permanently removes the files and the database now, and the domain can be used again. This cannot be undone.
sites.done.removed: Website deleted permanently. Its domain can be used again.
sites.done.remove_failed: The website could not be deleted. See the activity log.
sites.done.remove_confirm: Type the domain of the website exactly to delete it permanently.
dkey.title: Deploy key
dkey.add: This repository is private, so the panel made a key for this website only. Add it to the repository before you approve, so the first build can read it:
dkey.step.github: GitHub: the repository → Settings → Deploy keys → Add deploy key. Paste the key, leave "Allow write access" off.
dkey.step.gitlab: GitLab: the project → Settings → Repository → Deploy keys. Paste the key, leave "Grant write permissions" off. Bitbucket: Repository settings → Access keys.
dkey.step.then: Then press Approve and create here.
dkey.private: The private half never leaves this server; it is used only by this website's build.
dkey.hostkeys: Repository host key pinned on the first fetch:
dkey.nohost: The repository host key is pinned on the first fetch; a changed host key stops later builds.
rt.db.help: The app gets its own database on the private network, with DATABASE_URL and DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_NAME, DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD in its environment. Backups and the Database page cover it.
sites.creates.db.mariadb: Plus its own MariaDB database on the private network.
sites.creates.db.postgres: Plus its own PostgreSQL 18 database on the private network.
sites.resources.db.mariadb: The database adds up to 512 MB.
sites.resources.db.postgres: The database adds up to 512 MB.
db.rows.help.pg: Row counts are PostgreSQL estimates, updated by autovacuum and ANALYZE.
hook.title: Auto-deploy
hook.help: Deploy on every push to the branch %s. The repository calls this panel's webhook address; each delivery must carry this website's secret, and only a push to this branch starts a deploy. A push while another job runs waits for it.
hook.once: Copy the secret now: it is shown only this once. Making a new one stops the old one at once.
hook.secret.hidden: kept on the server (make a new one if it is lost)
hook.step.github: GitHub or Gitea: repository → Settings → Webhooks → Add webhook. Payload URL = the address above, Content type application/json, Secret = the secret above, event "Just the push event".
hook.step.gitlab: GitLab: Settings → Webhooks → Add new webhook. URL = the address above, Secret token = the secret above, trigger "Push events".
hook.step.then: Save. GitHub sends a ping first; it shows below as "ping". Then push to the branch.
sites.done.webhook-off: Auto-deploy turned off. Deliveries are refused from now on; you can delete the webhook at the repository.
php.db.help: The database runs on the website's private network. Your code finds it in the environment values DB_HOST, DB_NAME and DB_USER (with PostgreSQL also DB_PORT and DB_ENGINE); the password is in the file named by DB_PASSWORD_FILE. PostgreSQL adds the pgsql and pdo_pgsql extensions to PHP.
wp.db.only: Database: MariaDB (WordPress supports MySQL and MariaDB only).
sites.creates.laravel.pg: Database: PostgreSQL 18 instead of MariaDB; the PHP image also gets the PostgreSQL extensions.
img.title: Images
img.help: Every container runs an image pinned by its digest, never a floating "latest". A new panel version can carry newer pinned images (security fixes for PHP, WordPress, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, Nginx or a runtime); the website moves to them only when you press Update image.
img.how: Update image downloads the new images first (if that fails, nothing changes), makes a backup, then restarts the containers on them. If the website does not start healthy, the previous images are put back. The website is offline for a few seconds while its containers restart.
img.ask: Update this website to the new images? A backup is made first.
img.failhelp: If the new images did not start, the website runs on its previous images again. The backup made before the update is on the Backup page.
img.done: The website runs on the new images. The backup made before the update is on the Backup page, marked "before update".
sites.step.now.pull new images: Downloading the new images (the website keeps running)…
sites.step.now.build image: Building the image on the server (1–3 minutes)…
sites.step.now.recreate containers: Restarting the containers on the new images…
sites.app.uptime-kuma.help: Watches your websites and services (HTTP, ping, ports, certificates) and alerts you by Telegram, e-mail and more.
sites.app.n8n.help: Workflow automation: connect apps and APIs with a visual editor, webhooks and schedules.
ready.title: Ready apps
ready.help: A ready app runs its own official image, pinned by digest, with all its data in the website folder: the File Manager and Backup see it, and Update image moves it to newer versions the panel brings. You create its first account in the app itself.
ready.next.uptime-kuma: Uptime Kuma is running. Open it now and create its admin account: the first visitor sets it, so do it right away.
ready.next.n8n: n8n is running. Open it now and create its admin account: the first visitor sets it, so do it right away.
sites.creates.ready: One container: the app on its official image, pinned by digest, running as www-data with its data in the website folder; reachable only through the panel's HTTPS edge. It may reach the internet (checks, workflows). Backups stop it for a few seconds for a consistent copy.
sites.resources.ready: Up to 768 MB memory; disk grows with the app's data.
sites.busy.note: Working on the containers: usually a few seconds, up to 3 minutes while they report healthy. This page updates by itself when it is done.
lim.title: Resources
lim.help: Every website starts on our standard limits. Raise them only when this website needs more: memory is taken from the server only while it is used, the limit stops one website from taking all of it. Saving restarts the website's containers (a few seconds offline).
lim.php.help: Like cPanel's MultiPHP INI Editor. A higher memory_limit raises the memory of the containers that run PHP with it, so PHP always has room.
lim.total: Limits of all websites together: %s, server memory: %s.
lim.over: The limits add up to more than the server has: fine while the websites do not all use their full limit at once, but keep an eye on the Dashboard's memory.
sites.done.limits: Limits saved; the website runs with them.
disk.site.title: Disk usage
disk.site.help: Everything this website keeps on the server: its files, its database, its backups and the files deleted with the File Manager (kept 7 days).
disk.incomplete: The folder is very large: counting stopped after 20 seconds, the sizes shown are at least this much.
disk.tree.title: Largest folders and files
disk.name: Name
disk.more: %d more, smaller ones are not listed.
disk.big.title: Largest files
disk.big.help: Open a file's folder in the File Manager to download or delete it. Deleted files stay in the File Manager's trash for 7 days.
disk.server.title: Server disk
disk.sites.title: Websites
disk.docker.title: Docker
disk.docker.help: Images are the software of the websites (WordPress, PHP, databases, apps); the build cache speeds up building Laravel, PHP and app images. Older images stay after Update image so a website can go back.
disk.clean.images.ask: Remove every image no website names? Images of your websites (also WP-CLI and built images) stay. An older version kept after Update image is removed: going back then needs its backup.
disk.clean.help: Images named by a website and images a container uses are never removed. The build cache is rebuilt by the next build (it may take longer once).
engine.title: Engine
engine.docker.help: Every website gets its own containers: its own web server, PHP and database. The strongest separation between websites; about 150-250 MB of memory per WordPress at rest.
engine.native.help: The server's own Nginx, a PHP-FPM of its own that runs only while it serves visitors, and the shared MariaDB: a quiet website takes only a few MB. Separated by its own Linux user and sandbox, which is weaker than a container. WordPress, PHP and static websites only, always on Nginx, MariaDB only.
engine.native.php: PHP versions installed for the native engine: %s.
mig.title: Move a WordPress site here
mig.help: Bring an existing WordPress site into this website. It runs at %s first, so you can check it before you point the domain here. The old site is only read and keeps running.
mig.warn: The files and the database of this website are replaced by the old site's. A backup of this website is made first, so one restore brings it back.
mig.plugin.title: Way 1: the Nostek Migrate plugin
mig.plugin.s2: On the old site: Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin, choose the zip, then Activate.
mig.plugin.s3: Open Tools → Nostek Migrate there and copy the migration code.
mig.plugin.https: The old site must use HTTPS. The code is valid for 24 hours and stops working when the move is done; remove the plugin from the old site afterwards.
mig.code.need: Paste the migration code from Tools → Nostek Migrate on the old site.
mig.confirm: I understand the files and database of %s are replaced.
mig.confirm.need: Tick the box to confirm that this website is replaced.
mig.backup.title: Way 2: a cPanel backup
mig.backup.help: For hosting without SSH. In cPanel open Backup, then download a full backup, or the home directory backup together with the database backup. A zip or tar.gz of the WordPress folder with a .sql dump works too.
mig.backup.database: Database backup (.sql or .sql.gz), if it is a separate file
mig.type.archive: The backup must be a .tar.gz, .tgz, .tar or .zip file.
mig.type.database: The database backup must be a .sql or .sql.gz file.
mig.link.title: Or give a download link
mig.link.help: For a large backup: put it for a moment under the old site's public_html, or share it from cloud storage, and paste its https link. The server fetches it itself; remove the file from the old host afterwards.
mig.link.bad: The download link must be an https address.
mig.job.wait: You can leave this page; the move goes on in the background.
mig.job.done: The site has moved. Check it on the preview address, then point the domain at this server.
mig.job.next: The old site keeps running until the domain points here. Then open the Domains tab and press Check DNS again: the site moves to its domain. Remove the Nostek Migrate plugin from the old site.
mig.job.fail: The move did not finish. If this website looks wrong, restore its before-migration backup.
mig.choose.help: The backup holds more than one WordPress site (for example addon domains). Nothing was changed yet: choose the one to move.
mig.choose.need: Choose the WordPress folder to move.
mig.step.switch files: Website switched to the moved files
mig.step.addresses: Addresses changed to the new one
mig.step.now.switch files: Switching the website to the moved files…
mig.step.now.addresses: Changing the addresses to the new one…
dom.title: Domains
dom.help: Every name of this website, where DNS points it now and its certificate. A name is served once its A record points to this server (%s); the certificate follows within a minute. DNS itself stays at your domain's provider.
dom.col.name: Name
dom.why.ok: Served here, and DNS points to this server (%s).
dom.why.preview: The panel's preview address of this website; it points to this server (%s).
dom.why.moved: Served here, but DNS no longer points to this server (%s): visitors go elsewhere and the certificate cannot be renewed.
dom.why.ready: DNS now points to this server (%s). Press Check DNS again to serve it.
dom.why.mixed: Some A records point elsewhere. Keep a single A record with %s, then check again.
dom.why.elsewhere: DNS points to another server. Change its A record to %s at the domain's DNS provider, then check again.
dom.why.none: No A record. Add an A record with %s at the domain's DNS provider, then check again.
dom.why.error: The DNS lookup failed; try again in a minute. The A record should be %s.
dom.why.v6: An AAAA (IPv6) record points elsewhere: this server has no IPv6 yet, so remove it, or IPv6 visitors reach the other server and the certificate can fail.
dom.refresh.help: After you change DNS, press this: every name that now points here is served, and when the domain itself becomes the main address, WordPress's addresses move with it.
dom.refresh.ready: %d name(s) point here and can be served now.
dom.add.title: Add a name
dom.add.help: Like Aliases in cPanel: one more name for this same website (for example another domain or a subdomain). Point its A record to %s; until then it is listed but not served. Visitors of every extra name are sent to the main address.
dom.add.name: Name
dom.redir.title: Redirects
dom.redir.help: Like Redirects in cPanel: send visitors of one path elsewhere, to another path of this website or to another address. The query of the visit follows unless the target has its own.
dom.redir.301: 301 permanent (search engines move to the new address)
dom.confirm.need: Tick sure to remove the name.
dom.redirect.need: Enter both the path and where to send it.
dom.done.nochange: Nothing changed: no other name points to this server yet.
dom.job.cert: A new name gets its certificate within a minute or two; until then the browser can warn for that name.
dom.job.fail: The change was not applied; the website runs as before.
reveal.copyfail: Copy failed: the text is selected, press Ctrl+C
sec.title: Security
sec.help: Rules in front of this website, applied by the edge before a visit reaches the website, for every app and engine: blocked addresses, folders that ask for a login, and hotlink protection. A change takes a few seconds; a Docker website restarts its web container.
sec.job.fail: The change was not applied; the website keeps its previous rules.
sec.block.title: IP Blocker
sec.block.help: Like IP Blocker in cPanel: visits from these addresses get 403 Forbidden on every name of this website. One address or a network (CIDR), at most /8 for IPv4 and /16 for IPv6.
sec.ip.need: Enter the address or network to block.
sec.hot.title: Hotlink Protection
sec.hot.help: Like Hotlink Protection in cPanel: other websites may not embed this website's images and media (they get 403). Visits without a referrer (typed addresses, apps, most search engines) still work.
sec.hot.allow.help: One name per line, for example google.com. Every name of this website is always allowed.
sec.prot.title: Password-protected folders
sec.prot.help: Like Directory Privacy in cPanel: a folder of the main address (and everything under it) asks for a user name and password first. / protects the whole website.
sec.prot.note: A new user is added to the folder; an existing user gets the new password. The panel stores only a bcrypt hash of the password.
sec.protect.need: Enter the folder and the user name.
sec.pass.same: The two passwords are not the same.
sec.confirm.need: Tick sure to remove the protection.
files.ed.keys: Ctrl+S save · Ctrl+F find · Ctrl+Space suggest · Ctrl+/ comment · Alt+click more cursors
sec.err.title: Error Pages
sec.err.help: Like Error Pages in cPanel: turn a code on and the web server shows your own page for it. The pages are files in %s, edit them in the File Manager.
sec.err.note: A new page starts from a simple template; an edited page is never overwritten. WordPress and app frameworks show their own 404 page for their routes; these pages cover what the web server answers itself (missing files, 403, the app not answering).
sec.mime.title: MIME Types
sec.mime.help: Like MIME Types in cPanel: the content type the web server sends for a file extension, added to the standard list (an extension listed here replaces its standard type).
sec.mime.need: Enter the content type and at least one extension.
sec.noweb: Error pages and MIME types are for websites with their own web server (WordPress, PHP, Laravel, static). This app answers every request itself.
sec.scan.job.wait: Scanning the website's files. This can take a few minutes; you can leave this page.
sec.scan.job.done: Scan finished. The result is below.
sec.scan.job.fail: The scan did not finish. The reason is below.
sec.done.trashed: The file is in the file trash (restorable from the File Manager for 7 days).
sec.login.title: Login attempts
sec.login.help: Like cPanel's cPHulk history: every try to log in to this website (WordPress wp-login.php and xmlrpc.php, and the usual login pages of other apps), per address. Addresses that try a lot are guessing passwords: block them with one press.
sec.login.off: Not counting yet: the edge starts writing its access log after the panel update. Attempts show up here within a minute after that.
sec.login.none: No login attempts in the last 7 days.
sec.login.note: A failed login is visible for WordPress (the login form comes back) and when the app refuses (401, 403, 422, 429). Blocking adds the address to the IP Blocker above; your own address is shown there.
sec.scan.title: Malware scan
sec.scan.help: Like cPanel's Virus Scanner: ClamAV checks every file of the website for known malware (web shells, injected scripts, trojans). The files are only read; nothing is changed. A scan needs about %d MB of free memory and runs one at a time on the server.
sec.scan.failed: The last scan did not finish.
sec.scan.found: %d file(s) look like malware. Check each one; move it to the file trash if it does not belong to the website.
sec.scan.more: And %d more file(s) not listed: scan again after removing these.
sec.scan.note: A finding can be wrong (for example a security plugin's own sample files). After removing malware, change the website's passwords and update WordPress, its plugins and themes, then scan again.
sec.waf.title: Web application firewall (WAF)
sec.waf.help: Like cPanel's ModSecurity: every visit is checked against the OWASP Core Rule Set (Coraza) before it reaches the website. Attacks such as SQL injection, cross-site scripting, file inclusion and remote commands are found; in Block mode they get 403.
sec.waf.notready: The firewall service is not running on this server yet: it comes with the panel update.
sec.waf.p2: Stricter (level 2: more attacks found, more false alarms)
sec.waf.blocked: %d visit(s) blocked among the latest events
sec.waf.note: Start with Detect only for a few days: the events below show what would be blocked. Switch off a rule that hits normal use of the website, then choose Block. The first 128 KB of a form is checked; file uploads pass.
sec.waf.off.title: Rules switched off
sec.waf.skip.title: Paths not checked
sec.waf.rule.need: Type a rule number, for example 942100.
